title: You keep saying you’re ready for change.
paragraphs: You keep saying you’re ready for change.
But your mornings tell a different story.
The alarm goes off… and you hit snooze. Again. You promised you’d pray. You said today would be different. But instead, you scroll. Mindlessly. Quietly. Numb.
And you felt that little conviction, didn’t you?
That whisper.
This isn’t who you said you wanted to be.
But you ignored it.

God saw it.
You knew.

You say you want to break free from that sin, but you keep revisiting it like a familiar hiding place. You say you want discipline, but your habits are preaching comfort. You say you want God, but your time is being devoured by everything else.
And here’s what most people don’t realize…
Your habits are not neutral.
They are forming you.
Every small “yes” to distraction is a quiet “no” to transformation. Every delay, every compromise, every secret indulgence—it’s shaping your heart into something you never intended to become.

Jesus said,
“Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.” — Matthew 6:21
Read that again.
Your habits reveal your treasure.

Not your intentions.
Not your words.
Your habits.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
And that’s where it gets uncomfortable.
Because deep down, you know the gap is growing between who you claim to be… and who you actually are when no one is watching.

You sing the songs.
You repost the verses.
You say “God is good.”
But your private life?
It tells the truth.
“Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and not do what I tell you?” — Luke 6:46
That’s not a casual question. That’s confrontation.
That’s Jesus looking directly at the contradiction.

And suddenly, this isn’t about productivity anymore.
It’s about lordship.
Because change isn’t just about better habits.
It’s about a surrendered heart.

See, behavior modification can make you look cleaner…
But only the Gospel can make you new.

You don’t need a stronger routine.
You need resurrection.

Because the real issue isn’t that you lack discipline.
It’s that sin still has influence.
“For I do not do the good I want, but the evil I do not want is what I keep on doing.” — Romans 7:19
You felt that tension, haven’t you?
That internal war.
You want to change… but something keeps pulling you back.
That “something” has a name.
Sin.

And sin doesn’t just weaken you.
It enslaves you.
But here’s the turning point…
“Everyone who practices sin is a slave to sin… So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.” — John 8:34,36
Freedom is not found in trying harder.
It’s found in surrendering fully to Jesus Christ.
This is where everything shifts.

Because Jesus didn’t come to tweak your habits.
He came to destroy the power of sin over your life.

He lived the life you couldn’t live.
Died the death you deserved.
And rose again so you could become something entirely new.
“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.” — 2 Corinthians 5:17
Not improved.
New.
But you can’t step into new life while clinging to old patterns.
There’s a moment… right here… where you stop making excuses.

Where you stop blaming circumstances.
Stop waiting for motivation.
Stop pretending it’s not that serious.
And you face it.

You’ve been saying you want change…
But you’ve been resisting surrender.
And those are not the same thing.

One leads to frustration.
The other leads to freedom.
So now the decision is in front of you.

Not tomorrow.
Not “when things calm down.”
Now.
Will you keep living in the cycle—wanting change but choosing comfort?
Or will you finally lay it down?

The habit.
The sin.
The pride.
All of it.
Because Jesus isn’t asking for part of you.
He’s calling for all of you.
And if something in you is stirring right now… that’s not random.
That’s conviction.
Respond to it.

Say it plainly if you mean it—
“I’m done pretending. I surrender.”
There are people in your life who are stuck in the same cycle you’ve been in. Not to expose them—but to wake them up.
And if you’re serious about growing—about going deeper, being corrected, sharpened, and built in truth—there’s more waiting for you.
This is bigger than habits.
This is about your soul.
